tasks.short: Observe and evaluate students' work, determine progress and suggest improvements.

steps.what: Retrieve the student's actual prior work, current learning objectives and existing progress notes
inputs: existing learning objectives and progress notes
outputs: checked student work and learning context

steps.what: Observe the student's actual work and approach, asking questions where understanding is unclear
inputs: checked student work and learning context
outputs: actual observed work and demonstrated understanding

steps.what: Evaluate actual progress against objectives and decide useful suggestions for improvement
inputs: actual observed work and demonstrated understanding
checked student work and learning context
outputs: judged student progress and improvement suggestions

steps.what: Discuss the actual work and improvement suggestions with the student and check understanding
inputs: judged student progress and improvement suggestions
outputs: actual progress discussion and agreed practice

steps.what: Write the actual progress, suggestions and agreed practice note and check the completed note before retention
inputs: actual progress discussion and agreed practice
judged student progress and improvement suggestions

steps.what: Save the checked actual progress note in the same student record

tasks.design: Configure a student-scoped view of existing work and objectives in {LMS}, retaining manual fallback for paper work. Observation, progress judgement, feedback and actual note capture remain human; the same-record save earns no benefit.
tasks.previous_blocker: Existing work and notes can be separated across learner folders.
tasks.enabler_now: Native student filters can bring existing records together without evaluating the student.
tasks.still_hard: An answer alone does not show the student's understanding or next useful practice.
tasks.human_edge: The instructor notices how the student works and gives suitable personal feedback.

ambition.what: No automated learning assessment or grade.

tasks.altitude: Slightly less reference handling; teaching decisions are unchanged.

reach.task: Organise existing learner work for review

evidence.claim: Native learner views can retrieve existing work and notes without determining learning outcomes.

assumptions: Provisional shares cover work review, actual feedback and its existing note; no marking or official result transfer is included. s1 reads only existing student ID, work date, objective and prior note; the instructor locates paper/missing work manually within retained time.

s2-s5 capture actual observations, interpretation and agreed practice with full effort. No model infers ability or grades. s5 completes the note then checks it; an edit requires a fresh check before s6. Same-record save retains full human effort.
Try native student filtering before custom development. If the current view already works, only upkeep remains; no new learner capture work is assumed free.
unknowns: Existing work coverage and actual retrieval burden
research_questions: Does a native student view reduce total preparation when paper work is included?

already_counted.description: Actual progress note capture and factual check

incremental.description: Maintain student-view links and access settings

approvals.approved_version: actual progress note v1 completed and checked in s5

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: native learner retrieval already works, leaving half an upkeep hour. High: three reference-handling hours saved less half an upkeep hour; observation, assessment and feedback retain full effort.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Observe students to determine qualifications, limitations, abilities, interests and individual characteristics.

steps.what: Observe the actual student's participation and discuss their qualifications, interests and difficulties
Interpret the observed qualifications, limitations and abilities and distinguish evidence from uncertain impressions
Record the actual observations and their limits in the existing learner note and check the completed wording
Save the checked observation note to the same restricted learner record

tasks.design: Keep direct observation and interpretation human, including the actual learner note in {LMS}. A native note form is considered but it cannot supply observations or reduce the substantive wording check; no additional tool is proposed for this task.
tasks.previous_blocker: Understanding a student's abilities and limitations depends on situated evidence.
tasks.enabler_now: No demonstrated change shortens the actual observation, interpretation or short note here.
tasks.still_hard: Self-report, language confidence and observed performance can point in different directions.
tasks.human_edge: The instructor builds trust and avoids turning an uncertain impression into a fixed label.

ambition.what: No automated profiling or qualification decision.

tasks.altitude: No change in the instructor's week or authority for this task.

evidence.claim: Direct observation and contextual interpretation are needed to assess individual educational characteristics.

assumptions: Provisional shares explicitly separate observation, judgement, actual note writing/checking and save. No separate report, send or lookup is assumed; where one exists it needs its own timed step before estimation.

s1 instructor is the producer of actual observed behaviour and student-reported qualifications/interests; s2 produces the interpretation and uncertainty. s3 captures those actual facts manually, completes the note and checks it before s4; changed wording requires a new check.

The native learner-note form is already used and cannot infer actual observations. No speech recording, model assessment or new capture is introduced, so there is zero incremental upkeep. Same-record save retains full human effort. Progress-on-work evaluation in task6825 is a distinct case; any reused observation is allocated once in a roll-up.
unknowns: Whether a site requires additional formal observation reports or referrals
research_questions: Is there actual repeated transcription beyond the short existing observation note?

already_counted.description: Actual learner note authoring and factual check

incremental.description: No added tool or workflow, hence no incremental upkeep

approvals.approved_version: actual learner-observation note v1 checked after completion

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Both cases keep all actual observation, interpretation, note writing/checking and same-record save; no new mechanism supplies a saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Establish clear lesson, unit and project objectives and communicate them to students.

steps.what: Review actual learner needs and the applicable curriculum or course outcomes
Decide the intended lesson, unit or project learning objective and evidence of achievement
outputs: teacher-selected learning intent and achievement evidence

steps.what: Write clear learner-facing objective statements preserving the selected learning intent and evidence
inputs: teacher-selected learning intent and achievement evidence

loop.purpose: Reword teacher-selected objectives for the course's language level
loop.input: Teacher-selected intent, evidence, target language level and approved course vocabulary
loop.output: Plain objective statements preserving each selected learning demand
loop.check: Instructor verifies every statement keeps the intended skill, scope and success evidence; vocabulary checks alone are insufficient
loop.stop: One draft and one redraft, then teacher writes manually
loop.why_not_simpler: Where an approved objective bank does not fit, prose rewriting must preserve meaning while changing language complexity

steps.what: Read the completed objectives and approve the exact wording for this lesson and learner group
inputs: teacher-selected learning intent and achievement evidence

steps.what: Explain the approved objectives to the actual students and answer questions about what they will learn
outputs: actual communicated objectives and clarified expectations

steps.what: Save the approved objective version in the same course document

tasks.design: Use native course references and an approved objective bank in {DOCS} before a bounded language-rewrite loop. The instructor selects the learning intent, checks the finished wording, explains it in person and retains the approved version; no machine chooses learning demands.
tasks.previous_blocker: Objectives need language accessible to adult learners while preserving the intended skill.
tasks.enabler_now: Controlled references and bounded prose rewriting can reduce formulation effort.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing worthwhile, achievable objectives needs knowledge of actual learners.
tasks.human_edge: The instructor connects objectives to the learners' aims and explains unfamiliar expectations.

ambition.what: No expanded assessment or teaching authority is assumed.

tasks.altitude: Less wording work; objective selection and teaching remain human.

reach.task: Align learner-facing wording to selected course outcomes

evidence.claim: Bounded prose rewriting can propose simpler language but requires a teacher's meaning check.

assumptions: Provisional shares cover establishing and explaining objectives, not lesson delivery or grading. s1 uses existing teacher-produced learner needs and approved course outcomes; missing needs are established manually within retained time rather than inferred.

s2 supplies objective intent, scope and achievement evidence; s3 instructor supplies target language level and course vocabulary. Native search and approved statements are tried first. No student identifiers enter the rewriting loop.

s3 retained effort includes item-by-item meaning corrections. s4 checks the completed wording before communication and retention; changed text requires another check. s5 live explanation stays full and no electronic send is assumed. Same-document save earns no saving.
unknowns: Actual objective-bank coverage and rewriting correction effort
research_questions: Do rewritten objectives preserve the same learning demand at the target language level?

incremental.description: Maintain objective references and assess rewriting errors

approvals.approved_version: learner-facing objectives v1 checked in s4

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: unfamiliar objectives need full source review and rewriting, leaving upkeep only. High: six reference and7.5 wording hours saved less1.5 upkeep; objective choice and live explanation stay full.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Adapt teaching methods and materials to students' needs, abilities and interests.

steps.what: Decide the needed teaching-method or material adaptation from actual learner responses and course aims
Select the actual source material, target language level and examples suitable for the requested adaptation
Adapt the instructional text and exercises to the selected needs while keeping content and answer meaning intact

loop.purpose: Draft a bounded adaptation of selected instructional material
loop.input: Selected source, teacher adaptation brief, target language level and existing answer key
loop.output: Adapted text and exercises linked to source and intended skills
loop.check: Instructor reads every adapted item for factual fidelity, learning demand, accessible wording and answer correctness; flags changed meaning for correction
loop.stop: At most two redrafts then manual adaptation
loop.why_not_simpler: Rewording and choosing examples for a specified language level need semantic decisions; native formatting alone does not do that

steps.what: Check the finished material and approve its actual learning fit and the revised teaching approach
outputs: approved adapted material and teaching approach v1

steps.what: Try the adapted teaching approach with the actual learners and respond to difficulties in the moment
inputs: approved adapted material and teaching approach v1
outputs: actual adaptation trial and learner response

steps.what: Record the actual trial response and needed next change and check the completed adaptation note
inputs: actual adaptation trial and learner response
outputs: checked actual adaptation trial note v1

steps.what: Save the checked actual adaptation trial note in the same teaching document
inputs: checked actual adaptation trial note v1

tasks.design: Try the existing {LMS} material library and native editor first, using a bounded semantic rewrite only for teacher-selected adaptations. The instructor checks the completed material, tries the revised approach and captures the actual learner response afterward; a trial plan never becomes a completed result.
tasks.previous_blocker: Different reading levels and interests require repeated text adaptation.
tasks.enabler_now: Native lesson-editor rewriting can propose a different difficulty level under teacher review.
tasks.still_hard: Actual needs and in-class response determine whether an adaptation helps.
tasks.human_edge: The instructor notices frustration, confidence and misunderstanding and changes approach appropriately.

ambition.what: Prepare checked versions of a selected activity for an additional reading level in the same class.

tasks.altitude: More preparation options; live adaptation and responsibility remain human.

evidence.claim: LessonUp's lesson editor can rewrite text at another difficulty and produce vocabulary lists; this supports draft adaptation, not learning judgement.

assumptions: Provisional shares. Scope is adapting selected methods/materials and checking an actual trial; it does not claim routine lesson delivery or student assessment savings. If observation overlaps task6836, allocate the observation once in a roll-up.

s1 instructor supplies actual need, course aim and adaptation intent. s2 supplies source text, target language level, suitable examples and any existing answer key; missing source/answers are resolved manually within retained effort. No learner profile or answer key is invented and no identifiers enter the loop.

s3 retained60% includes semantic review and corrections, with s4 final whole-material check. s5 actual trial stays full and s6 actual response capture follows it. Changed material needs another s4 check before use; changed actual note needs another s6 check before s7.
No electronic publication/send is included; any later handout release requires its own action and final-version gate. Same-document save retains full human effort and earns no saving.
unknowns: Actual share of adaptation effort spent rewriting versus live method changes
research_questions: Can the instructor verify meaning and answers faster than adapting the text manually?

already_counted.description: Final adapted material and approach check
Actual post-trial response capture and factual check

incremental.description: Maintain adaptation settings and review recurring rewrite failures

approvals.approved_version: actual adaptation trial note v1 completed after actual trial in s5

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: source cleanup and correction remove all preparation benefit, leaving upkeep. High: three source-selection and twelve text-adaptation hours saved less two upkeep; live trial, actual capture and same-document save remain full.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The instructor retains direct observation and teaching while spending less time locating work and rewording selected learning materials.
role.ambitious_version: Offer checked material variants for more learner needs while retaining human learning decisions and live support.

job.title: Adult Basic Education, Adult Secondary Education, and English as a Second Language Instructors
